title: nerve
content_html:
nerve

The word can mean a pathway for sensation, a tender point or the courage to do something. All three senses meet in a reading of Nerve and nerve forms. Where does a sensation travel, where does it become an image, and where does the speaker find the nerve to put it into words? The Library’s account of bodily signalling sits alongside the felt experience of being touched, shocked or exposed. Pain and shock can make it hard to say where bodily sensation gives way to psychological disturbance. The imagery of healing and purification in Nerve gives that bodily vulnerability another language. Nerve · Brain signals

Reading note. Buddhism. In the discourse on the two arrows, one arrow represents bodily pain and the second the mental distress that can follow. In Nerve, a sensation can acquire a memory, a fear or a story. The arrows offer a way of asking how these experiences come together, even where the passage leaves them difficult to distinguish. Sallattha Sutta, SN 36.6
